passages.note: Aye vote on AB 1279 concurrence; the bill's operative text (see companion snapshot) declares an emissions-reduction policy achievable by carbon capture, not a clean-energy mandate.

passages.provision_quote: It is the policy of the state to do both of the following: (1) Achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions as soon as possible, but no later than 2045, and to achieve and maintain net negative greenhouse gas emissions thereafter.
passages.note: The bill also directs the state board to enable 'carbon dioxide removal solutions and carbon capture, utilization, and storage technologies,' so the target names no energy source and can be met without a clean-energy shift.

rows.reasoning: AB 1279's operative text declares 'the policy of the state' to reach net zero emissions by 2045 and directs the state board to pursue that goal in part through carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture technologies, naming no energy source. That is an emissions target achievable by means other than a shift to clean energy, not the rung 1 mechanism ('Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines'), so Lee's Aye vote on this single-subject bill shows only the pro-action side.
